root_cause: When a focused element inside the focus trap is removed from the DOM, the browser moves focus to the document body. The focusin handler (checkFocusIn) detects focus on the body but the trap's mostRecentlyFocusedNode still references the detached element. The recovery logic in the else branch attempts to focus the detached node, which fails, leaving focus on the body. Additionally, the previous fix attempted to use an isNodeAttached utility that is not defined in the focus-trap module, causing a runtime error.
repair_strategy: Define a local isNodeAttached helper in the focus-trap module that checks node attachment (including shadow DOM). Then modify checkFocusIn to clear the mostRecentlyFocusedNode when it becomes detached, and in the Document focus branch, restore focus to the initial focus node when the MRU node was detached.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus remains trapped inside the dialog after removing an item, preserving tab order and preventing focus loss to background elements.
functional_risks: The isNodeAttached check may have performance implications if called frequently, but it's only on focusin events. It correctly handles shadow DOM and detached nodes.
The Document focus restoration might trigger on legitimate temporary Document focus (Firefox iframe) if the MRU node is detached for other reasons, but the detached-node check mitigates this.
verification_requirements: After pressing Enter on the remove button of an item, the count updates and focus stays inside the basket (#basket:focus-within is true).
Tab navigation continues to wrap correctly within the dialog after item removal.
